title: Operational rhythm & SLO rollout roadmap — cross-team initiatives 2025
summary: Practical, timeboxed plan to operationalize service-level objectives across product, infra, and SRE teams. Focus: short feedback loops, measurable SLO adoption, predictable on-call rhythms, and integration with Redwood Console dashboards.
objectives: Define and publish per-service SLOs for top 10 customer-facing endpoints (latency + availability) by end of Q2 2025
Establish an operational cadence (weekly/biweekly checkpoints) with Product, Infra, Observability, and Console before Q3 2025
Automate 80% of alert-to-owner routing and create runbook templates for SLO breaches
Instrument Redwood Console with token-level cost/latency overlays for SLO triage
milestone_timeline: 2025-02-15: Program kickoff — cross-team goals aligned (SRE + Observability + Product + Infra)
2025-03-01: Inventory completed — candidate services, SLIs identified (latency P50/P95, error-rate)
2025-03-18: Draft SLO bundles for top 5 services; internal review with Product
2025-04-08: Runbook templates and alerting rules first-pass deployed to staging
2025-05-12: Console dashboards with SLO health and cost overlay beta
2025-06-30: Publish SLOs for top 10 endpoints; begin canary enforcement and postmortem integration
owners_and_roles: Asha Patel — Program lead (SRE): coordination, program metrics, exec updates
Marco Liao — Observability lead: SLIs, dashboarding, metric hygiene
Priya Sen — Product infra partner: SLO alignment to product priorities, rollout decisioning
Diego Alvarez — Serving runtime engineering: instrumentation hooks, perf baselines
Emma Zhou — Console & Insights: dashboard UX, tracing links, SLO exports
workstreams: SLI definition & validation: identify signals, ingestion paths, cardinality controls, sampling guidance
SLO authoring & policy: templated SLOs, error budget rules, enforcement thresholds
Alerting & routing: group alerts by SLO impact, auto-assign owners, integrate with PagerDuty rules
Runbooks & playbooks: short remediation steps, escalation matrix, postmortem checklist
Console integration: SLO health tiles, cost/latency overlays, per-token traces to SLO breaches
Training & onboarding: runbook dojo, tabletop exercises, office hours for teams
checkpoints_and_rituals: Weekly SLO standup (30m): blockers, quick wins, action items — attendees: owners + product reps
Biweekly cross-functional review (60m): milestone status, risk review, resource requests
Shadow incident rotation: SRE + Product observer to refine runbooks (2-week pilots)
Monthly exec snapshot: top-level SLOs, error budget burn, customer-impact incidents
acceptance_criteria: Per-service SLOs published in Confluence and wired into Redwood Console
End-to-end alert flow validated in staging with auto-assignment to on-call
At least 3 tabletop exercises completed with <30% first-run failures on procedures
Metric cardinality and cost controls in place (estimated <10% ingestion cost increase)
SLO breach postmortems automatically linked to incident records and tagged
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Metric explosion causing cost overruns — Mitigation: enforce cardinality limits, sampling guidance, and review gate for new SLIs
Risk: Product teams resist strict SLOs due to feature velocity concerns — Mitigation: opt-in canary enforcement and alignment to business KPIs
Risk: Alert fatigue from naive thresholds — Mitigation: use error-budget-driven paging and set MTTx targets for noisy signals
Risk: Console integration slips due to UX changes — Mitigation: early API contract and stub dashboards for validation
open_questions: What is the cutover policy if a published SLO causes frequent pager noise? (escalation path)
How do we represent multi-model endpoints (hosted + dedicated variants) within a single SLO?
Do we require product sign-off for every SLO change or only for SLA-impacting thresholds?
What storage/retention window do we need for SLI history to support quarterly regressions?
